concepts.title: Line of Sight and Horizontal Level
concepts.definition: The line of sight is the line drawn from the eye of an observer to the point in the object viewed. The horizontal level is the horizontal line through the eye of the observer.
concepts.key_idea: The line of sight and the horizontal level form the angle of elevation or depression at the point of observation.
question_patterns: identify the line of sight in a given situation
distinguish between line of sight and horizontal level
draw the line of sight for an observer looking at an object
identify the horizontal level in a heights and distances problem

solution_steps.explain: Locate the eye of the observer and the point being viewed.

solution_steps.action: Draw the line of sight and horizontal level
solution_steps.explain: The line of sight joins the eye to the object. The horizontal level is the horizontal line through the eye of the observer.
The angle between the line of sight and the horizontal level is the angle of elevation (object above) or depression (object below).

worked_examples.question: An observer looks at the top of a tower. Identify the line of sight and the angle formed.
worked_examples.solution: The line from the eye of the observer to the top of the tower is the line of sight. The angle between this line and the horizontal level is the angle of elevation.

worked_examples.question: From the top of a cliff, an observer looks at a boat. What is the line of sight and the angle called?
worked_examples.solution: The line from the eye on the cliff to the boat is the line of sight. The angle between this line and the horizontal level is the angle of depression.

concepts.title: Angle of Elevation
concepts.definition: The angle of elevation of an object viewed is the angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal level when the object is above the horizontal level.
concepts.key_idea: The angle of elevation is measured upward from the horizontal to the line of sight.
question_patterns: find the angle of elevation given height and distance
identify the angle of elevation in a diagram
compute angle of elevation using trigonometric ratios
determine angle of elevation from top of a building
find angle of elevation when observer moves closer or farther

solution_steps.explain: The height, the horizontal distance and the line of sight form the triangle.
tan(theta) = height / distance.
The elevation angle is the inverse tangent of height/distance; use tables or a calculator.

concepts.title: Angle of Depression
concepts.definition: The angle of depression of an object viewed is the angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal level when the object is below the horizontal level.
concepts.key_idea: The angle of depression is measured downward from the horizontal to the line of sight, and equals the angle of elevation from the lower point.

tan(theta) = height / distance for the depression angle.

concepts.title: Finding Height of an Object Using Angle of Elevation
concepts.definition: The height of an object can be found using the angle of elevation and the known distance from the observer to the base of the object.
concepts.key_idea: In the right triangle formed, tan of the angle of elevation relates the height to the horizontal distance.
question_patterns: find height of a tower given angle of elevation and distance
find height of a building using angle of elevation
compute height of a pole from a measured distance
find height of a mountain using angle of elevation
determine height of a flagstaff using trigonometry

solution_steps.explain: Tower height is opposite; ground distance is adjacent to the elevation angle.
tan(angle) = height / distance.
height = distance x tan(angle).

concepts.title: Finding Distance Between Two Objects
concepts.definition: The distance between two objects can be found using angles of elevation or depression measured from a point of known height.
concepts.formula: distance = height * (cot(alpha) - cot(beta)) or height / tan(angle)
concepts.key_idea: When two objects are observed from the same elevated point at different angles, the distance between them is found using the difference of cotangents.
question_patterns: find distance between two objects observed from a height
compute distance between two cars using angles of depression

determine distance between two boats using angles of depression

solution_steps.explain: From the tower top, each depression angle gives a right triangle sharing the same height.
Each base distance equals h / tan(angle).
Farther base distance minus nearer base distance is the gap between the objects.

concepts.title: Word Problems on Heights and Distances
concepts.definition: Heights and distances problems apply trigonometric ratios to real-world situations involving finding heights of objects or distances between points using angles of elevation or depression.
concepts.formula: height = distance * tan(theta); distance = height * cot(theta)
concepts.key_idea: Translate the word problem into a right triangle and apply the appropriate trigonometric ratio.
question_patterns: solve word problems on heights and distances

determine the distance of a ship from the shore
find the height of a cloud using angle of elevation

solution_steps.explain: Convert the word problem into a labelled right triangle.
Pick the ratio that links the two known sides with the unknown.
Substitute the values, solve for the unknown and check the size of the answer.

worked_examples.question: A tree breaks due to storm and the broken part bends so that the top touches the ground making an angle of 30 degrees. The distance between the foot and the top is 10 m. Find the height of the tree.
worked_examples.solution: Let the standing part be h and broken part be x. tan(30) = h/10, so h = 10/sqrt(3) = 5.77 m. cos(30) = 10/x, so x = 10/cos(30) = 11.55 m. Total height = 5.77 + 11.55 = 17.32 m.

concepts.title: Using Trigonometric Ratios in Right Triangles to Solve Real-World Problems
concepts.definition: Trigonometric ratios sin, cos, and tan relate the sides of a right triangle to its angles and are used to solve real-world heights and distances problems.
concepts.formula: sin = opposite/hypotenuse; cos = adjacent/hypotenuse; tan = opposite/adjacent
concepts.key_idea: Choose the appropriate ratio based on which sides are known and which is to be found.
question_patterns: use sin ratio to find height or hypotenuse

solution_steps.explain: Opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse relative to the given angle.
sin for opposite-hypotenuse, cos for adjacent-hypotenuse, tan for opposite-adjacent.
Solve the ratio equation for the unknown side.

concepts.title: Problems Involving Two Right Triangles
concepts.definition: Some heights and distances problems require setting up two right triangles sharing a common side, typically the height of a tower, with two different angles of elevation.
concepts.formula: height = d1 * tan(alpha) = d2 * tan(beta); d1 + d2 = total distance
concepts.key_idea: When two angles of elevation are measured from two points on opposite sides of a tower, the height is found by equating the two expressions for height.
question_patterns: find height of tower given two angles of elevation from opposite sides
find distance between two observation points using two angles
solve problems with two right triangles sharing a common height
find height when two angles of elevation and total distance are given
determine the height of a tower from two points on the same line

solution_steps.explain: Two observation points give right triangles sharing the tower height h.
d1 + d2 = D for points on opposite sides; d2 - d1 = D for the same side.
h = D / (cot(alpha) + cot(beta)) across the tower; h = D / (cot(alpha) - cot(beta)) on one side.

worked_examples.question: Two points on opposite sides of a tower are 50 m apart. The angles of elevation from these points are 30 and 60 degrees. Find the height of the tower.
The angles of elevation of the top of a tower from two points at distances 4 m and 9 m from the base (same side) are complementary. Find the height of the tower.
worked_examples.solution: Let angles be theta and 90-theta. tan(theta) = h/9 and tan(90-theta) = h/4, so cot(theta) = h/4. Thus h/9 * h/4 = 1, so h^2 = 36, h = 6 m.
